session_cue.text: "Ow, why did you do that?" - Squints

previous.text: Father William marked the witch's home and the Barrow Mound on the party's map.
Trout recruited Squints, a halfling newly arrived in town, into his Halfling Corps as a junior assistant.
Trout and Dr. Uriah caught Naggeneen the Clurichen, who had been stealing Quinn's alcohol, in the Golden Egg's basement.
Dunk scouted Warwick the smith's shop at night and spotted a magical mithril chain shirt.
Dunk agreed to help Ingrid the Alchemist drug Warwick with a sleeping potion. He then gave her watered-down faun wine to make it.
George, who lost his arm to the dragon, told the party where its lair lies and how it killed his friends.
After Father William's account of Brandon's sword, the party set out through the woods for the Barrow Mound.
The party chose a route to the Barrow that avoids the house of Vivian, the witch.
Dr. Uriah agreed to give penance and money for the Barrow Mound at Father William's request.
Dunk drank the fauns' wine without effect and traded a rabbit's foot for a faun's flask of wine.
Dr. Uriah and Ingrid agreed Father William is the worst, and Ingrid denied his claim about her potions.
Squints pulled a captive Brother Dirk from a giant's cottage, and the party outran the waking giant.

current.where_you_are: The party is in the woods north of town, across the field from the giant's stone cottage after outrunning the giant. Squints and the rescued Brother Dirk are with them.

immediate_intention.text: The party is heading to the Barrow and is pressing Brother Dirk to come along instead of going home. Trout has told Dirk he will report to Squints.

Your goals.text: Find the treasure the party seeks.
Kill the black dragon near Brandonsford and drag its body into town for Eric the Reeve's 1000 gold bounty.
Obtain Warwick the smith's magical mithril chain shirt.
Duel Eric the Reeve at dawn, if Sir Phidipaldi still means to press his challenge.

Standing in your way.text: George says nothing pierces the black dragon's scales, its poisonous bite kills, and it spits sulfur. His group's arrows and swords all failed.
Eric the Reeve has not accepted Sir Phidipaldi's dawn duel. He is offended by Sir Phidipaldi's false claims about George's dragon and the glove slap.

What could help.text: If the party pays Lady Hilda, a seasoned armored fighter, she will join their dragon hunt.
If Dunk helps Ingrid dose Warwick with her sleeping potion, Dunk can get into the house unnoticed. The diluted faun wine may weaken the potion.
Father William says that if the party retrieves Brandon's sword from the Barrow Mound, they will have the only weapon that can kill the dragon. George says no one knows if the legend is true.
If the party pays Drop Dead Ned 100 gold a week, he and his killer wasp will do anything that lets him kill. He refunds 5 gold per kill if he can do what he wants with the bodies.
Dunk says he has a plan to get Warwick's mithril chain shirt. If he gets it, it could help against the dragon.

Still unanswered.text: Why has nothing come into Brandonsford for months?
Why are fairies that once stayed hidden now coming out more often?

Promises and debts.text: Dunk must help Ingrid get her sleeping potion into Warwick's house and give it to Warwick.
Dr. Uriah must donate 10 gold to Father William for the Barrow Mound's upkeep.
Dr. Uriah must give penance at the Barrow Mound, as Father William asked.
Trout owes Squints second pick of treasure after the elite members once the party finds its first treasure. Until then Squints funds himself.

Meanwhile.text: George says the black dragon cannot fly yet but soon will, and then Brandonsford is doomed.
The man-eating giant in the stone cottage north of town is unharmed and may capture and eat anyone passing near.

facts.text: Find the treasure the party is seeking.
The party holds a treasure map marking several locations they don't recognize; they assume the treasure is probably at one of them.

classification.support_basis: The map narrows the treasure to a few marked places, though the party cannot yet identify them and only assumes the treasure is at one.

facts.text: Where does the treasure lie?

classification.grounding_justification: The session explicitly frames the map's locations as unrecognized and the treasure's place as only assumed to be among them.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Identifying the marked places and which holds the treasure requires more than one lookup but is mainly a location fact.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Finding the treasure's location is useful and central to the quest but chiefly instrumental.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Unfamiliar land and several marked sites naturally support asking locals and exploring to match them.

facts.text: Where did the treasure map come from?

classification.grounding_justification: Dr. Uriah tried to recall the map's history and knew nothing; the gap is noted but nothing makes it strange.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Learning the map's origin could explain who hid the treasure, but play suggests nothing concealed.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mildly interesting background, mainly useful for locating the treasure.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: No source or lead about the map's origin has been established.

facts.text: The party plans to check out a marked map location on their walk to the Barrow.
facts.uncertain_reason: The beats do not say whether the giant's cottage the party found on the way was the marked location, or whether the check is still to come.

classification.support_basis: Visiting a marked site lets the party test whether the treasure lies there, narrowing the search among the unrecognized locations.
classification.action_basis: The party agreed on the route and holds the map with marked locations along it; the visit needs only walking there.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: walking to a marked location en route to the Barrow. Benefit: checking whether the treasure is there, which largely amounts to pursuing the want itself.

facts.text: Dr. Uriah plans to secretly copy the party's map during his downtime.

classification.support_basis: A copy would give Uriah his own version of the map, but play established no specific advantage it brings toward finding the treasure.
classification.action_basis: Uriah carries the map and can copy it, but no concrete advantage toward the treasure was established.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: Uriah copying the map. Benefit: none named beyond holding a copy.

facts.text: Reginald the frog says a little trickster creature called a Clurichen comes from the riverbanks into town every night, up to no good, and that the party should stay away wherever it goes.
facts.ended_how: no longer relevant: the Clurichen, Naggeneen, was caught and hangs in a bag behind Quinn's bar

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: The creature is only said to be 'up to no good' and to be avoided; no specific harm is named.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: It is described as a little trickster; nothing suggests more than mischief or minor harm.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: Rests on a single warning from a river frog, unconfirmed by observation.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: Reginald describes a nightly pattern of the creature coming into town, so the visits are ongoing.
classification.preventability_justification: The party can heed the warning and avoid it, or watch for it at night, though no specific means is established.

facts.text: What does the Clurichen do when it comes into town at night?
facts.ended_how: answered: Naggeneen drinks Quinn's alcohol in the Golden Egg's basement

classification.grounding_justification: Reginald says only that it is 'up to no good', leaving its actual activity unstated; the question is suggested rather than framed.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal the creature's hidden nightly activity, a hidden circumstance in town.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mildly interesting; could explain local mischief but nothing established ties it to other events.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Could be investigated by watching the town at night or questioning locals, supporting some lead-following.

facts.text: Naggeneen the Clurichen, hanging in a bag behind Quinn's bar at the Golden Egg, offers his pot of gold or a secret to whoever lets him go.
facts.uncertain_reason: Sir Phidipaldi refused the offer and Naggeneen is now Quinn's captive; unclear whether the offer still stands.

classification.support_basis: No established want or debt of the party is served by gold or an unspecified secret.
classification.action_basis: Naggeneen offered gold or a secret for release, but no want it advances is established and freeing him would mean taking Quinn's captive.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: releasing Naggeneen from the bag. Benefit: a pot of gold or a secret, which names no advantage toward any established want or debt.

facts.resource_subject: Naggeneen held in a bag behind Quinn's bar

facts.text: What does Quinn intend to do with the captured Naggeneen?

classification.grounding_justification: Quinn pointedly says he knows what he will do with the Clurichen without saying what, and the bag still hangs there next morning.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: A single statement of Quinn's intention would settle it.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mildly interesting fate of a captive fairy; mainly incidental.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Answerable by asking Quinn or watching the tavern.

facts.text: Kill the black dragon near Brandonsford and drag its body into town to collect Eric the Reeve's 1000 gold bounty.
Lady Hilda would join the party's dragon hunt for pay.

classification.support_basis: A seasoned, armored fighter would strengthen the party against the dragon.
classification.action_basis: Hilda explicitly offered to join adventurers hunting the dragon for money.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: hiring Hilda; benefit: an experienced armored fighter for the dragon fight.

facts.text: The woodsman George, who lives a couple of houses from the Clumsy Fox, encountered the black dragon and lost an arm to it; the party could ask him where he met it.
facts.ended_how: used up: Sir Phidipaldi questioned George about the dragon

classification.support_basis: A firsthand account could help the party find and prepare for the dragon, though George's willingness is not established.
classification.action_basis: Eric says George lives nearby and might come by tonight; he is an eyewitness, though he has not offered help.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: questioning George; benefit: where and how he met the dragon, helping the party locate it.

facts.text: Where did the black dragon come from?

classification.grounding_justification: Its lair is now known, but George says only Sir Brandon killed the dragon ages ago, Gill earlier called this a different dragon, and Ingrid links its arrival to fairies encroaching.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Answering could reveal why a dragon appeared after centuries, beyond a simple location.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Its origin may connect to Brandonsford's dragon history, but mainly it is instrumental for the hunt.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: George, Gill's fairytales and Ingrid are sources.

facts.text: George says the black dragon cannot fly yet but soon will, and then Brandonsford is doomed; it has already killed George's companions.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: George names a specific outcome: the town's destruction once the dragon flies.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: Doom of the whole town and already several deaths.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: Rests on the testimony of George, a survivor, but is unconfirmed.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: George describes an advancing process (it will soon fly), but gives no timeline or observed signs.
classification.preventability_justification: Killing the dragon before it flies would prevent it, but it requires Brandon's sword, which is not yet recovered.

facts.classification_change_basis: Beat_48 raises the harm from maiming individuals to the town's doom once the dragon flies, so severity rises from medium to high.

facts.text: George says the dragon's lair is up north at the foot of the mountains, reachable without climbing.

classification.support_basis: Knowing where the lair is lets the party find the dragon, though the location is only roughly given.

facts.text: George says nothing pierces the black dragon's scales, its poisonous bite kills, and it spits sulfur; his group's arrows and swords all failed against it.

classification.scope_basis: These are the dragon's own traits and will apply in any fight with it.

facts.text: Father William says the dragon cannot be killed without the magic sword buried with Brandon in the Barrow Mound.

classification.support_basis: The sword is said to overcome the dragon's invulnerability, though George says no one knows what is true of the legend.
classification.action_basis: The party has decided to walk to the Barrow Mound to retrieve the sword.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: recovering Brandon's sword from the Barrow Mound; benefit: a weapon said to be able to kill the otherwise unkillable dragon.

facts.resource_subject: Brandon's sword as the only means of killing the dragon

facts.text: Can Eric the Reeve actually pay the 1000 gold bounty?

classification.grounding_justification: George explicitly says he doubts Eric has 1000 gold.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: A single check of Eric's means would settle it.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mainly practical, though it could expose Eric as dishonest.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Little beyond asking or checking Eric's resources.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi vowed to George to bring his lance against the dragon, after George said he could repay him by killing it.

classification.stake_basis: George only remarked that a lance was untried and wants the dragon dead; nothing shows he relies on the lance specifically.

facts.text: George says a lance, which Sir Phidipaldi carries, is one of the few weapons never tried against the dragon.

classification.support_basis: Only an untested possibility; George doubts it, and other accounts say only Brandon's sword can kill the dragon.

facts.text: Dunk says Warwick's mithril chain shirt could help against the dragon, and he has a plan to get it.

classification.support_basis: Magical armor would offer some protection in the dragon fight, though nothing shows it resists the dragon's poison bite or sulfur.
classification.action_basis: Dunk has seen the shirt in Warwick's shop and says he has a plan to obtain it.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: obtaining Warwick's mithril chain shirt; benefit: magical armor for a fighter facing the dragon.

facts.text: Lady Hilda, a seasoned fighter who says she can't hunt the dragon alone, offers to join the party for money to hunt it.

classification.support_basis: A seasoned armoured fighter would add real combat strength to a party seeking to kill the dragon for the Reeve's bounty, though her fee is unset.
classification.action_basis: Hilda explicitly offered to join a party of adventurers for money, and her fighting ability matches the need to kill the dragon.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: hiring Hilda for pay. Benefit: an experienced fighter's help in killing the dragon. Evidence: her own offer in the prior Session.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi told Lady Hilda the party would talk with the Reeve and come back to take up her services.

classification.stake_basis: This was a statement of intent to return; nothing shows Hilda relies on the party coming back or would be wronged if it didn't.

facts.text: Drop Dead Ned offers himself and his killer wasp for hire at 100 gold a week, doing anything as long as he gets to kill; he will refund 5 gold per kill he is allowed if he can do what he wants with the bodies.

classification.support_basis: Ned adds a willing killer and a killer wasp to a party pursuing a dragon bounty, though nothing shows he or the wasp could harm a dragon.
classification.action_basis: Ned explicitly offered his services for 100 gold a week, and killing is what the dragon bounty needs, a straightforward capability-to-need match.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: hiring Ned for 100 gold a week. Benefit: an extra killer with a killer wasp toward killing the dragon for the Reeve's bounty. Evidence: Ned's offer and stated killing capability (beat_21, beat_22).

facts.text: Why has nothing, including Bentley's restock shipment, come into Brandonsford for months?

classification.grounding_justification: Two independent sources earlier said shipments have stopped, and this Session the narration confirms shipments still have not come in. The cause is never stated.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal an underlying cause, such as an interruption on the roads, that the town has not identified.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Bentley set the stoppage beside the dragon rumors, so the cause could explain the town's wider troubles. That link is only suggested.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: It could be pursued by following the supply route and questioning merchants and townsfolk.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi wants to fight Eric the Reeve in a duel at dawn.
facts.uncertain_reason: The challenge was one-sided and Eric never accepted; play has not shown whether Sir Phidipaldi still means to press it after being sent to the Golden Egg.

facts.text: Eric the Reeve, offended by Sir Phidipaldi's false claims about George's dragon and the glove slap, did not accept the dawn duel, saying only that Sir Phidipaldi is more skilled at adventure.

classification.scope_basis: Eric's refusal and offense were left unresolved when Bentley separated them, and the duel was set for the following dawn, so the refusal outlasts the tavern scene.

facts.text: Buy Shamus the mule from Farmer Gill, who asks 100 gold.
Farmer Gill would accept killing the dragon outside town as work in trade for Shamus instead of 100 gold.

classification.support_basis: It offers an alternative price for Shamus if Dunk lacks 100 gold, though the dragon hunt is a large and dangerous undertaking.
classification.action_basis: Gill said, when Dunk asked about trading work, that the big work needed was killing the dragon.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: killing the dragon. Benefit: it pays Gill's price for Shamus in place of gold. This simply meets the want's own terms of sale.

facts.text: Farmer Gill won't lower his price for Shamus until his sons come back, since he can't work the farm without them or a mule; his sons are away hunting the dragon.

classification.scope_basis: Gill's condition depends on his sons returning from the dragon hunt, which is ongoing beyond the scene (beat_2, beat_67).

facts.text: Help Quinn get back at Bentley, whom Quinn blames for stealing his ale at night, and collect Quinn's 100 gold.
facts.ended_how: achieved: the ale thief was caught and Quinn paid Sir Phidipaldi, Trout and Dr. Uriah 33 gold each; the thief proved to be Naggeneen, not Bentley

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi and Quinn agreed to stage a fake ale shipment: Quinn brings bottles to fill with water and Sir Phidipaldi makes a big show of delivering them.
facts.ended_how: obsolete: the thief was caught in the basement without the fake shipment

classification.support_basis: With no real shipments arriving in town, a showy fake delivery of watered bottles gives the night thief bait, setting up Quinn's revenge; whether it works is untested.
classification.action_basis: Quinn and Sir Phidipaldi explicitly agreed to the plan and Quinn will supply the bottles.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: staging the fake delivery; benefit: baiting whoever steals Quinn's ale so he can get back at them; linked by the agreement in beat_36.

facts.text: Who or what empties Quinn's good stock at the Golden Egg every night?
facts.ended_how: answered: the thief is Naggeneen the Clurichen, who drinks to unwind at night

classification.grounding_justification: Quinn describes a strange nightly pattern of a full bar becoming half-empty or knocked-over glasses by morning, and only suspects Bentley without proof.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer reveals a hidden culprit and their method behind a recurring anomaly.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Identifying the culprit would explain the mystery and may overturn Quinn's accusation of Bentley.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Supports a stakeout, the fake-shipment bait and questioning townsfolk.

facts.text: Under the Halfling Corps terms, Trout owes Squints second pick of treasure after the elite members once the party finds its first treasure; until then Squints funds himself.

classification.stake_basis: Squints agreed to join, fund himself and take Trout's orders specifically in exchange for this pick of the first treasure.

facts.text: Squints, a halfling fighter with a sling and dagger who is more experienced than Trout, has joined Trout's Halfling Corps and takes orders directly from Trout.

classification.support_basis: An extra experienced fighter who agreed to fight monsters adds modest combat and stealth help toward the dragon hunt, though nothing suggests he can hurt the dragon.

facts.text: Obtain Warwick the smith's magical mithril chain shirt.
Warwick sleeps in a second-story bedroom of his shop-home with the window cracked open at night.

classification.support_basis: The open upstairs window is a physical way into the house where the shirt is kept, though it leads into the room where Warwick sleeps.
classification.action_basis: Dunk saw the window cracked open; climbing in is a physical option, and Ingrid already climbs to that sill nightly.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: entering through the open window at night. Benefit: access inside the closed shop-home where the shirt is displayed. Evidence: beat_16.

facts.text: Dunk's sleeping-potion deal with Ingrid could put Warwick to sleep and get Dunk inside his house.

classification.support_basis: A drugged Warwick and help getting inside would let Dunk reach the shirt unnoticed, though the potion is not yet made.
classification.action_basis: Ingrid agreed to work on the potion and Dunk proposed helping her inside to give it to Warwick; Dunk told the party he has a plan to get the armor.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: completing the potion and going in with Ingrid. Benefit: Warwick asleep and unable to wake while Dunk is inside. Evidence: beat_28, beat_64.

facts.text: What magic does Warwick's mithril chain shirt hold?

classification.grounding_justification: The shirt glows and is clearly magical, but its properties were never stated or framed as a mystery.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Identifying an item's property is a simple fact.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Settled by examining or identifying the item.

facts.text: Dunk is to help Ingrid get her sleeping potion into Warwick's house and give it to Warwick, so she can watch him all night without fear of him waking.

classification.stake_basis: Ingrid is making the potion on the understanding that Dunk will get it inside, which serves her wish to watch Warwick without being discovered.

facts.text: Ingrid is making a sleeping potion from Dunk's diluted faun wine; Dunk can collect it at her shop (she said tomorrow, he said tonight) and use it to keep Warwick asleep while they are inside his house.

classification.support_basis: A sleeping Warwick lets Dunk enter the house where the mithril shirt hangs, though the diluted wine may weaken the potion.
classification.action_basis: Ingrid agreed to make the potion and told Dunk to return for it; the plan has Dunk entering Warwick's house with her.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: collecting the potion and dosing Warwick; benefit: Warwick stays asleep so Dunk can get into the house unnoticed; linked by Dunk's plan and Ingrid's agreement.

facts.text: Dunk knows Ingrid secretly climbs to Warwick's window nightly to leave gifts and watch him sleep, which she dreads him learning; she says she owes Dunk for keeping it secret.

classification.support_basis: The secret gives Dunk leverage to keep Ingrid cooperating with getting him into Warwick's house.

facts.text: Will Ingrid's sleeping potion work, given Dunk diluted the faun wine to about one part in five?

classification.grounding_justification: Dunk deliberately diluted the key ingredient heavily, clearly raising whether the potion will work.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: A single test of the potion settles it.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mainly practical for the armor plan.

facts.text: Can Ingrid really make her own potions? Father William says she is incompetent and cannot; Ingrid says she makes all her products herself.

classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer could reveal whether someone else, such as the witch Vivian, supplies her potions.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Could expose a hidden relationship behind her shop, though mostly it bears on the potion's reliability.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Could be pursued by watching Ingrid or visiting Vivian.

facts.text: The fauns of the Faun Grove, north of town across the river, trade their wine, which makes almost any non-faun drunk from a sip, for sentimental items such as a love letter or a pixie's treasure.

classification.support_basis: More undiluted faun wine would let Ingrid remake the sleeping potion if the diluted batch fails.
classification.action_basis: The fauns already traded Dunk a flask for a rabbit's foot and say they trade for sentimental items.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: trading a sentimental item to the fauns; benefit: full-strength faun wine, the potion's key ingredient, so the sleeping potion can be made reliably.

classification.action_basis: The Barrow is marked on the party's map about three miles away and the party has set out for it; the sword would let them harm the otherwise unpierceable dragon.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: retrieving the sword from the Barrow Mound. Benefit: a weapon said to overcome the dragon's invulnerability. Linked by Father William's and George's accounts of Brandon's sword.

facts.text: Father William marked the Barrow Mound on the party's map; it is roughly a three-mile walk north through the forest.

classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Confirming or debunking the Brandon legend would be mildly interesting but is mainly instrumental.

classification.opening_basis: Trigger: asking Farmer Gill about the Brandon fairytales. Benefit: lore about the sword that could help the party find or use it. Linked by George's remark.

facts.text: What is the coven Father William says Vivian and Ingrid share?

classification.grounding_justification: Father William claims a coven; Ingrid calls Vivian a friend and frames witchcraft as a reclaimed word and a forest religion repressed by the church, leaving the relationship's nature unclear.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal a hidden relationship and practice between the two women.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Could reveal a secret religious circle, mildly changing understanding of Ingrid and the town's tensions.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Ingrid, Father William and Vivian's marked home are sources that could be questioned or visited.

facts.text: Why, as Ingrid says, are fairies that used to stay hidden now encroaching and coming out more often near Vivian's forest home?

classification.investigative_depth_justification: The cause would explain a broader change in the region, possibly tied to the dragon.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Could connect to the fairy-given sword legend and the dragon, a meaningful revelation.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Ingrid, Vivian and the forest itself offer leads to follow.

facts.text: The man-eating giant in the oversized stone cottage in the woods north of town is unharmed after the party took Brother Dirk from it, and may capture and eat anyone passing near it.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: Dirk says the giant was going to eat him in its stew, so the harm is being captured and eaten.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: The party saw Dirk bound in a sack beside the giant's cooking pot and Dirk testifies to its intent, but whether it will threaten the party again is not directly shown.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: The giant had already captured a traveller and chased the party, but nothing shows it hunting them now; it tired and gave up.
classification.preventability_justification: The giant is slow and was easily outrun, and the party knows where its cottage is and can avoid it.
